title: Opponent misreads Dort V.9 as equating assurance with divine-faith certainty
source_text: CXXXV. Porro ex hac Doctrina Theologorum Britannorum, secundum quorum suffragia conditi sunt Canones Synodi Dordracenae, & quorum hocce judicium actis, ut dixi, Synodi illius insertum est, colligere licet quanta cum ratione vir ille Doctus qui meas Theses carpit, profert verba ejusdem Synodi, quasi definierit persuasionem quam habent fideles de gratia & salute propria, esse ejusdem rationis, firmitatis, & certitudinis cum divina illa fide, qua fidei articulis immediate a Deo revelatis assentimur. Verba unde istud exsculpere conatur, habentur in quinto doctrinae capite, articulo nono, qui sic habet: De hac electorum ad salutem custodia, veraeque fidelium in fide perseverantia, ipsi fideles certi esse possunt, & sunt, pro mensura fidei, qua credunt se esse & perpetuo mansuros, vera & viva Ecclesiae membra, habere remissionem peccatorum, & vitam aeternam. Quibus verbis judicet lector; An definitum sit fidem qua fideles certi sunt, se remissionem peccatorum & vitam aeternam habere, aequalis esse certitudinis, firmitatis & necessitatis cum divina illa fide, qua praecipuis fidei articulis assentimur? Et num verisimile sit virum Doctum melius sensa Dordracenae Synodi percipere; quam illos ipsos qui ad conficienda ejus decreta operam contulerunt, & primi illis subscripserunt?
pass_a_gloss: Further, from this Doctrine of the British Theologians — according to whose votes the Canons of the Synod of Dort were framed, and whose this judgment, as I said, is inserted in the acts of that Synod — one may gather with how much reason that Learned Man who carps at my Theses brings forward the words of the same Synod as if it had defined that the persuasion which the faithful have concerning their own grace and salvation is of the same kind, firmness, and certainty with that divine faith by which we assent to the articles of faith immediately revealed by God. The words from which he tries to carve that out are found in the fifth chapter of doctrine, article nine, which runs thus: Concerning this custody of the elect unto salvation, and the true perseverance of the faithful in faith, the faithful themselves can be, and are, certain, according to the measure of faith, by which they believe that they are and will perpetually remain true and living members of the Church, have remission of sins, and eternal life. By which words let the reader judge: Has it been defined that the faith by which the faithful are certain that they have remission of sins and eternal life is of equal certainty, firmness, and necessity with that divine faith by which we assent to the chief articles of faith? And is it likely that the Learned Man perceives the sense of the Synod of Dort better than those very men who contributed labor to composing its decrees and first subscribed them?
pass_b_english: Given that the British deputies' votes shaped Dort's Canons and their judgment stands in the acts, the opponent has little ground to read Dort V.9 as defining own-grace persuasion equal in kind and certainty to divine faith in immediately revealed articles.

Dort V.9 says the faithful can and are certain, according to the measure of faith, that they remain living church members, have remission, and eternal life — not that this certainty matches assent to the chief revealed articles.
Readers should ask whether the carping Learned Man reads Dort better than the deputies who drafted and first signed its decrees.

lemmas.gloss: fifth chapter of doctrine, article nine
according to the measure of faith

rejected: Dort equates assurance with dogmatic certainty
